faq.a: 90° and 180° rotations are lossless — pixels are simply rearranged. Custom angle rotations use high-quality bicubic interpolation, which may introduce very slight softening at extreme angles. For most purposes, the quality is excellent.

faq.q: Will my image be uploaded to a server?
faq.a: No. All processing happens entirely in your browser using the Canvas API. Your images never leave your device. There is no server that receives or stores your files.

faq.q: What happens to the canvas size when I rotate?
faq.a: For 90° and 270° rotations, the canvas width and height swap to fit the rotated image perfectly. For custom angles, the canvas expands to contain the entire rotated image, and the background color fills any new space.

faq.q: Can I rotate and flip at the same time?
faq.a: Yes. Set your rotation angle first, then click a flip button. The flip applies on top of the current rotation. Both transformations are combined in the final output.

faq.q: What's the difference between rotating 180° and flipping vertically?
faq.a: Rotating 180° turns the image upside down (top becomes bottom, left becomes right). Flipping vertically only mirrors top-to-bottom (left stays left). They produce different results unless the image is perfectly symmetrical.
You can upload a GIF, but only the first frame will be rotated. The output will be a static image (PNG, JPG, or WebP), not an animated GIF. For animated GIF rotation, a specialized tool is needed.

faq.q: Is there a file size limit?
faq.a: There's no artificial limit, but very large images (over 50 megapixels) may be slow to process in the browser. Most photos from phones and cameras work instantly.
